Priya (Support): Customer acme-corp reports repeated failures when using structured_output (json_mode). They see parse errors from the client, then multiple automatic retries -> big billing spike. Also the customer claims some calls returned 401 during retries. Can we triage?

Alex (Support): Thanks — can you paste a redacted request + the raw response body they got? model + deployment name + json_mode setting?

Priya (Support): Pasting minimal repro (redacted):

```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-1.0",
  "json_mode": "strict",
  "prompt": "Generate a JSON object with keys foo and bar",
  "max_tokens": 60
}
```

Response body they received (raw):
```
{"foo": "ok", "bar": "value",}
```
(note trailing comma). Client's pydantic decode fails and their SDK retries. Also saw some 401s in logs after a retry spike.

Jin (Eng-ML): Trailing comma is valid JS but not strict JSON. With json_mode=strict we validate at the edge and then return parse error? We should check whether the model output has stray control chars (e.g. \u0000) or mismatched brackets. Can you share the full raw response with headers?

Priya (Support): Attached headers from our logs: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, x-customer-id: acme-123. Response had content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8 and content-length 32. Raw bytes snippet shows 0x7d 0x2c 0x0a ("},\n").

Maria (Eng-Platform): Noted. Two separate issues: 1) model emitted non-strict JSON (trailing comma) -> pydantic/jsonschema downstream parse fails. 2) SDK retry behavior + transient auth 401s -> billing. Immediate mitigation: we can flip customer account to json_mode=relaxed for their routes which will attempt an auto-cleanup step (strip trailing commas, fix common JS-isms) before returning. That should stop client-side retries.

Alex (Support): Do we have a documented escape hatch we can toggle per-account? I can apply if we agree. Also need a short message to the customer explaining a temporary setting change + ask them to confirm they can retry once we flip it.

Jin (Eng-ML): For longer term, runtime should sanitize model output before we hand it to the API layer when json_mode==strict. Proposed small patch: a sanitizer that removes trailing commas, converts single quotes to double quotes where safe, and rejects control chars. I'll open a PR with unit tests using examples. Canary deploy tonight if no red flags.

Priya (Support): Customer is asking for repro steps so they can test locally. Can you provide a curl they can run that reproduces the trailing comma behavior?

Jin (Eng-ML): Sure — use this to simulate server output (we run a toy stub):

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","json_mode":"strict","prompt":"return {\"foo\":\"a\",\"bar\":\"b\"}"}'
```

The staging runtime will replay an example model output with a trailing comma so they can test client behavior.

Alex (Support): Also, note that different schema validators behave differently: pydantic (strict) fails fast with a JSONDecodeError — message we saw: `Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes` — whereas some JS zod schemas will accept JS-style objects if the client uses eval-like parsing. We should add a note to our docs in the structured-output troubleshooting section about validator interoperability and recommend customers use a post-fetch normalization step if they rely on strict libraries.

Maria (Eng-Platform): Agreed. Action items:
- (Maria) Toggle json_mode=relaxed for acme-123 right now (temporary).
- (Jin) Open PR for sanitizer + unit tests (target: canary tonight).
- (Alex/Priya) Tell customer we've applied the temporary change and ask them to retry; collect any SDK stack traces.
- (Support Bot) Create internal ticket and link PR/issue.

Support Bot: Ticket created: #SUP-3421 -> "structured_output: trailing-comma causes pydantic failures + billing due to retries". Assigned to Eng-ML.

Priya (Support): Done — told customer we toggled relaxed mode and asked for a repro run. They ran their suite and confirmed retries stopped and no 401s seen in the next hour. They still want an engineering fix so they can go back to strict.json_mode.

Jin (Eng-ML): Will prioritize the sanitizer PR. One note for implementers: avoid over-normalizing (don't auto-fix deeply ambiguous structures). The sanitizer should include a best-effort header: `X-Redwood-Json-Sanitized: true` when fixes applied so downstream can audit.

Alex (Support): I'll update the support ticket and close after PR merges and we confirm with customer. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Maria (Eng-Platform): Follow-up doc TODO: add a short interop guide: "How to make json_mode strict play nicely with pydantic/zod/jsonschema" with examples and recommended SDK hooks.

Priya (Support): Closing loop with customer now. Will paste customer confirmation into SUP-3421 once they reply.

Jin (Eng-ML): Quick note for the PR description: include a small test matrix: model outputs with trailing comma, stray 0x00, single quotes, and missing quotes. That will cover the most common real-world model emission errors.

Alex (Support): Copy.

Priya (Support): Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for the audit trail.
